name: Aamchee
description:
Aamchee is a pure vegetarian restaurant in Gamdevi, South Mumbai, specialising in authentic Mumbai breakfast and comfort food. Known for misal pav, poha, upma, vada pav and pav bhaji, we serve fresh, homestyle Maharashtrian favourites every day.

Located near Chowpatty, Babulnath and Kemps Corner, Aamchee is a go-to spot for veg breakfast, quick bites and casual dining. The menu also features chaat, South Indian dishes, coffee and light meals, with Jain-friendly options available.

Clean, family-friendly and centrally located, Aamchee is ideal for dine-in, takeaway and delivery.

featured_reviews.name: sachin kamat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Form is awesome, content needs to match up to it & this team can do it!

Here are the things we loved :
- imaginative menu
- lovely ambiance
- friendly staff
- comes with an awesome reputation
- the Mahabaleshwar patties was super

Here are things that can be better:
- thanks to the reputation & first hand experience of Soam the expectation is very high and any lapse can make a big difference
- the food needs to match - the menu which is very thoughtful : few examples (1) Bharli Vangi served needed to be authentic, for the promise, expectation and price - what was served was deep fried brinjals mixed with green masala, which had lots of oil floating on it : Expectation was authentic stuffed / bharli brinjal (2) The Grandma’s fresh green chana - when we checked was dried green chana soaked overnight! The promise and the delivery needs to match (3) the Maharashtrian platter was super greasy and soaked in oil (4) The portions are abysmal- the Potli Biriyani was minuscule & the Jowar Roti accompanying the Bharli Brinjal were a tad bigger than poories!

All in all - you have built a great reputation, you have an awesome venue, we know you have the capability - please please please deliver on the quality, authenticity and portions of the food - that’s what we come there for in the first place

Please see this as a fans review - I want to come there often and enjoy the menu you have promised!

featured_reviews.name: Bomi Manekshaw
featured_reviews.review_text:
The concept of a high tea unlimited buffet would seem attractive to the Indian pallet. Most food items like the two bite burger or the singal piece sev puri are certainly not items to be eaten cold and stale in a buffet.
The service was pleasent but excruciatingly slow for the 90 plus year old ladies who visited more for the experience than to demonstrate their poor appetite. The only item that they thought would be worth having with a hot coffee or tea were the bhajiyas.

And, the staff tested the ladies patience of taking almost 30 minutes plus to heat and serve them. Thank God the flavour of the mango mousse in the tiny cutting chai glass was the saving grace for these oldies. But, at ₹725/- (including taxes) per person this was certainly more premium a price for being next to the Bhavan's and Wilson College clientele than the food, service or lounging.

While the decore has some antique stuff like the ancient telephone ... overall they have the opportunity to work a lot on the atmosphere too.

We ordered Veg Kolhapuri, Roti, and Jeera Rice. The Veg Kolhapuri was perfectly spiced, with a rich, thick gravy loaded with fresh vegetables. The spice level was just right—not too mild, not overly spicy—giving it an authentic Kolhapuri taste. The rotis were soft, freshly made, and paired well with the curry. The Jeera Rice was well-cooked, aromatic, and light, making for a great combination with the sabzi.

The restaurant was clean and well-maintained, with a simple but comfortable dining setup. Since it’s near Mumbai Central, it gets quite busy, but the service was decent quick and efficient. The staff were polite and ensured we had a smooth dining experience.

The pricing is quite high, and the portion sizes are satisfying. Whether you’re travelling through Mumbai Central or looking for a good vegetarian meal in the area, Shiv Sagar is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Shubham Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Crystal Restaurant at Chowpatty is one of those classic places in Mumbai that has built its reputation over many years by serving consistently good food. Located close to the famous Girgaon Chowpatty, it’s a convenient spot to visit after enjoying the sea breeze or an evening walk on the beach.

The restaurant is known mainly for its simple yet delicious North Indian and vegetarian dishes. Their Punjabi thali, dal makhani, paneer preparations, and butter rotis are especially popular among regular customers. The food is rich in flavor, well-cooked, and feels like traditional home-style North Indian cuisine. Portion sizes are also quite generous, making it a good value-for-money place, especially if you’re dining with family.

One thing that stands out about Crystal is its old-school charm. The interiors are simple and not overly fancy, but the place has a warm and nostalgic feel that many longtime visitors appreciate. The staff is generally polite and efficient, and even during busy hours they try their best to serve quickly.

Another positive point is the location. Being so close to Chowpatty makes it a great stop for a proper meal after having street food or spending time by the beach. Many locals and tourists visit this restaurant when they want something more filling than snacks.

However, during peak hours the place can get quite crowded, and you might have to wait for a table. The ambiance is also more traditional than modern, so those expecting a luxury dining experience might find it a bit basic.

Overall, Crystal Restaurant is a reliable place for tasty North Indian vegetarian food in the Chowpatty area. If you’re looking for comforting meals, generous portions, and a classic Mumbai dining experience, it’s definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Ankit Davda
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you want to experience old-school Mumbai charm with soulful food and timeless vibes, then Crystal Restaurant Chowpatty is a place you simply cannot miss. Located exactly opposite Girgaon Chowpatty near Wilson College, this iconic decade-old restaurant carries the true essence of vintage Mumbai. The moment you walk in, it feels like stepping into a different era — simple interiors, retro atmosphere, classic old Hindi songs playing softly in the background, and that comforting feeling modern cafés often fail to give.
What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. Perfect spot after a long Marine Drive walk or a relaxed dinner with family and friends. The combination of Chowpatty breeze, retro Bollywood music, and homely Punjabi-style food creates an experience that feels warm and memorable.

What makes this place special is not fancy presentation or luxury décor, but the authenticity. The vibe here is peaceful, nostalgic, and beautifully old-fashioned. Perfect spot after a long Marine Drive walk or a relaxed dinner with family and friends. The combination of Chowpatty breeze, retro Bollywood music, and homely Punjabi-style food creates an experience that feels warm and memorable.
The food is genuinely amazing and surprisingly affordable considering the location. Their North Indian dishes taste rich, comforting, and consistent — proper “ghar jaisa but better” flavors. The ghee chapati, paneer dishes, rajma chawal, dal tadka, parathas, and especially the famous rice kheer are absolutely worth trying. Portions are satisfying and pricing is one of the best around Marine Drive-Chowpatty area.  
The Times of India +2
Unlike many overhyped places around Marine Drive, Crystal still holds onto its original charm. No loud music, no unnecessary flashy interiors — just good food, retro songs, old Mumbai energy, and a beautiful comforting atmosphere. You can actually sit peacefully, enjoy conversations, and soak in the nostalgic vibe. Many locals and old Mumbaikars still consider it one of the hidden gems of South Mumbai.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

We also decided to try the Jowar pita pocket which was good but could do with less mayo. Overall it's good to try the gujarati dishes, though it is on the pricey side.

featured_reviews.name: Indradeep Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Valet parking is available. It’s a pure Veg restaurant and being a prolific meat eater I was reluctant to visit to begin with. However, when I stepped out of the restaurant I had eaten to my hearts content and was super happy. Thus, I think it’s worth everyone to visit and try out. The food was very different to the ones we are accustomed eating

I actually started with dessert and ordered a special of the day which was served on a milk base.

Then I ordered the Oondhiya. Normally it’s served with puri , but I requested only the sabzi and i relished it completely. I would surely recommend to try it.

We also had Gatte ka sabzi and Satpadi which was quite nice as well. It was served on dried loaves that was placed over plates. Innovative way to keep the plates cleaner and easy to wash.

I guess a visiting once again to try out a few more dishes in the future

featured_reviews.name: Jay Haria
featured_reviews.review_text: The mutter paratha with aloo-dahi sabzi was comfort food done well, balanced and not oily. The mutter pattice had a crisp exterior with a fresh filling, and the panki was soft and fragrant as expected. The guava drink added a refreshing, mildly sweet finish.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cream Centre — A Nostalgic Delight with Exceptional Chole Bhature.

From the moment we stepped into Cream Centre, we were transported into a warm, nostalgic world — and what a delicious journey it turned out to be. This iconic vegetarian restaurant, with its rich legacy (dating back decades) , continues to deliver comfort food that feels both familiar and special.

If you’re looking for the ultimate chole bhature experience, Cream Centre should be on your list without question. Combine that with their nachos, cheese corn balls, and sizzling brownie, and you’ve got a meal that’s fun, indulgent, and full of heart. For us, it wasn’t just a meal — it was a love letter to Mumbai’s vegetarian dining culture. Highly recommend, and we’ll definitely be back.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hey Adnan Khan
The nostalgic atmosphere and exceptional food you experienced at Cream Centre truly warm our hearts. It’s wonderful to hear that our chole bhature, alongside the nachos and cheese corn balls, made such a delightful impression. We look forward to welcoming you back for more of those memorable meals that celebrate the essence of Mumbai’s vegetarian cuisine.
Regards,
Team Cream Centre

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Parulekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a vegetarian and not going to Cream Centre Chowpatty… what are you even doing with your life? 😄

This place has one of the most happening menus ever like you open it and suddenly everything looks like your “all-time favourite.” Total confusion but the good kind.

First rule: DO NOT leave without trying the Ice Cream Soda. Seriously. Missing that would be a personality flaw at this point 😅

Their menu is a crazy (and amazing) mix of Italian + Indian. My absolute favourite? Chole Puri Cheese Tacos yes, it sounds wild, but trust me, it works like magic. Also try the Potato Crispers and Cheese Nachos… they’re dangerously addictive.

Pro tip: They have Zomato Pay, so check your cards for discounts and feel like a smart saver while eating like a king 👑

Special shoutout to Mr. Thomas absolute legend! He helped us with ordering, gave great suggestions, handled everything smoothly and made sure we were happy throughout. Honestly, half the good experience was because of him. Thomas, if you’re reading thisTHANK YOU and we’re coming back just for you 😄

Overall: Amazing food, great vibe and zero regrets. This is one of those places where you go once… and then keep finding excuses to go again.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hey Pooja Parulekar
Your enthusiasm for our menu is infectious! It's wonderful to hear that you enjoyed the fusion of Italian and Indian cuisine, especially the Chole Puri Cheese Tacos and the addictive Potato Crispers. 
Regards,
Team Cream Centre

featured_reviews.name: Shruti Trehan
featured_reviews.review_text: Cream centre chowpatty is a Mumbai landmark - a rare pearl in the Queen’s necklace or Marine Drive. The menu has expanded to cater to the new generations but the traditional signature dishes like Chole Bhature and street food such as pani puri or dough balls filled with myriad chutneys and lentils, sizzlers taste exactly the same - they are perfect! The accompaniments including the pickled carrots crunchy spicy and tangy are a feast for the senses. And of course no trip to Bombay in the summer months is complete without the Alfonso mango the king of all fruits and they celebrate this with a separate menu offering various delectable options starting with the basic Aamras which is simply golden mango puree to mango ice cream to mango pina colada and so much more! Out service was outstanding, the interior was clean and comfortable and our server Bikash was attentive yet not intrusive!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hey Shruti Trehan
Your description of our Cream Centre Chowpatty truly captures its essence as a beloved gem along Marine Drive. It’s wonderful to hear that our menu, with both classic and modern flavors, met your expectations so perfectly. The mention of our mango offerings being a highlight is especially delightful, as we take pride in celebrating the king of fruits during the summer months. 
Regards,
Team Cream Centre

featured_reviews.name: Selvamanojkumar S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cream Centre at Chowpatty, an iconic restaurant to enjoy a delicious vegetarian food. It was a surprise that they maintain the perfect balance between Indian and foreign cuisine with utmost justice. The portion is good, their homemade Nachos became my favourite and really taken back by the taste of the pasta.

The place easily get crowded and be prepared for a waiting time of 30-40 minutes depending on the crowd. It took 30 mins to get a seat on a Thursday night dinner for us. The service could have been better, as they get confused of orders and their respective seats. Despite all this, I will definitely visit to taste their other listings in the menu and to get surprised by their taste. A definitely recommended one for scrumptious food.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:

Thank you for your kind words about the delicious vegetarian food and the homemade nachos! It's wonderful to hear that you enjoyed the unique flavors we offer. We understand that the wait can be challenging during busy hours, and we’re actively working on streamlining our service to ensure a smoother experience for our guests. We look forward to welcoming you back to explore more of our menu!
Regards,
Team Cream Centre

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sunday brunch at this Rooftop Cafe was a symphony of flavors, sounds, and warmth.

The anti-pasti spread was a visual feast, with a colorful array of dips, cheeses and salads. Each bite was a masterclass in textures and flavors, with the perfect balance of tangy, spicy, sweet and savory notes. Total hit. Must try.

The refreshing mocktails were the perfect accompaniment to the meal, with unique flavor combinations that tantalized my taste buds.

The mains however could have been better. The spaghetti aglio e olio was dry and little overcooked.
The nachos were delicious.
The potato Rosti was loaded with black pepper making it difficult to eat.

The desserts were good.

The live music added a delightful ambiance with the musician's soulful voice.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a leisurely and indulgent weekend treat.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently discovered Cafe Calma, nestled in the iconic Shalimar Hotel, Kemps Corner, and I'm still reeling from the experience!

Ambience: 5/5
The rooftop setting offers breathtaking views of the city, making it perfect for a relaxing Sunday Brunch.

Food: 5/5
The unlimited antipasti spreads are a game-changer! With new themes every week, you'll get to indulge in a variety of flavors, from classic Mediterranean to modern European.

Service: 5/5
The staff is warm, attentive, and knowledgeable. They'll ensure you have a fantastic time!

Value for Money: 5/5
At ₹2000 per person, this Sunday Brunch experience is a steal!

Overall, Cafe Calma is a must-visit for anyone looking for a tranquil dining experience with great food, stunning views, and exceptional service.

Will I return? Absolutely!

The Kairi Kanda Roomali and Pakoda made for a great start and disappeared almost instantly. The Paneer Kairi Tikka stood out with its soft texture and well balanced flavours, easily one of the highlights from the menu.

The beverage selection complements the theme well. Options like the Mango Frozen Margarita and Mango Passion Fruit Mojito are refreshing, while the Mango Lassi is a great pick if you are in the mood for something richer and more filling.

Moving to the mains, the Paneer Khada Masala with Garlic leaves a strong impression and ranks among the better versions you will come across. It fits perfectly into the kind of comforting, flavourful food this place is known for.

Desserts keep things traditional and satisfying. The Gulab Jamun paired with Lacchedar Rabdi works beautifully, while the Aamras Puri is an easy choice, especially during the season.

What makes Revival stand out is how easy it is to return to. It is the kind of place that works just as well for a casual meal as it does for a family outing, and even welcomes your furry companions.

Conveniently located a short walk from Charni Road station, and set within a heritage building just off the Chowpatty seaface, it is a spot that is both accessible and consistently dependable when you are in the mood for good, comforting food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointing Experience on Diwali
We were a group of 5 who had booked a table a day in advance through Google for 20th Oct, 9pm. On calling the restaurant in the afternoon about parking, the manager suddenly claimed they have “stopped online reservations” — even though the slot was available and confirmed on Google. When I asked his name (atleast thriceA) he disconnected the call without telling.
Not taking a chance, we reached at 7:30pm. The restaurant was barely 40% occupied. Our waiter Kabir was polite and helpful — full marks to him for service.
The major issue happened at billing — they flatly refused to accept Zomato payment despite Zomato showing a good discount option. There was no notice displayed, and we were not told at entry or while ordering. The manager “Shrikant Pedhnekar” was unapologetic and defensive instead of clarifying or expressing regret. While we were leaving, another manager (name unknown) also argued with us. In this era of 'Customer First', not once these managers showed any signs of being apologetic nor regret. The high-handed attitude spoiled our mood. Especially when the prices are comparable with premium restaurants. While prices match that of premium restaurant, the customer-centric attitude does not.

Other aspects:
• Ambience feels dated — furniture and décor easily 15–20 years old
• Prices are comparable to premium restaurants but food is only average in taste and portion
• We ordered for two cocktails but they were not well made.
• Service charge of 10% was added automatically while most restaurants of this level charge 5% (we got it removed)
• Restaurant is on 1st floor - No lift so elderlies and people with mobility issues will find it difficult to reach the restaurant

Overall, good food and smiling service of Kabir the waiter saved complete disaster. One star is for him. 4 stars goes out for an unprofessional and disappointing handling of guests. Would not recommend until management fixes confirmed reservations, billing transparency and how they treat their customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

🔹 *Benne Dosa*: Soft, buttery, South Indian heaven!. The benne (butter) was rich and aromatic - loved it!
🔹 *Farm Fresh Pizza*: Wait, a farm-fresh pizza inside a temple? 🤯! Toppings were fresh, crust was spot on 🍕. Got the vibe that the ingredients were picked fresh for the temple devotees... felt special!

Eating amidst the temple's vibes, felt like a foodie blessing 🙌. Service was super attentive 😊.

If you're around Iskon anywhere in the world, Govinda's is an absolute MUST 📍. Blend of divine vibes + tasty food = recipe for a soulful meal 👌."

Dakshinayan is a small but excellent South Indian restaurant in Walkeshwar. The dosas are consistently good, the food quality is solid, and the service is quick and efficient.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Gujarati feast with a seasonal twist, Gujju Bhai No Thali is absolutely worth a visit right now!

The highlight of the experience is their unlimited aamras, served fresh as a summer special—and honestly, it steals the show. Sweet, rich, and perfectly chilled, it pairs beautifully with their hot, fluffy puris… pure comfort on a plate.

The thali itself is incredibly wholesome and satisfying. It starts off with refreshing drinks like chaas and pudina pani, setting the tone for what’s to come. The appetisers—kachori, dhokla, and chaat tart—are all fresh and flavourful, giving you that perfect mix of crunch, spice, and tang.

Moving to the mains, you’re treated to four different sabjis, two dals, and a classic Gujarati kadhi that strikes the perfect balance of sweet and tangy. Pair these with soft phulkas or puris, and it’s a complete meal in itself. You also get options like jeera rice and comforting dal khichdi, which just add to the homely feel of the meal.

And just when you think you’re done, the desserts keep coming! From warm halwa to the indulgent malai sandwich, everything feels like a celebration of flavours.

Overall, Gujju Bhai No Thali delivers a hearty, value-for-money dining experience with that signature Gujarati hospitality. With the mango season in full swing, the unlimited aamras makes it even more special—definitely not to be missed!
